title: Build your query and set the condition

blocks.content:
You'll build a query that watches QuickPizza for server errors, then confirm when the alert fires.

Use **Builder** mode instead of writing PromQL. Keep the condition as **Is above** **0**.

On the **New alert rule** page, choose the data source that holds the metric you want to alert on.

**grafanacloud-play-prom** is filled in for you.
blocks.tooltip: Prometheus data source from the QuickPizza tutorial data sources.

blocks.content: Optionally, toggle **Explain** on. Grafana describes each part of your query in plain language.
Confirm **Builder** is selected so you can build the query without writing PromQL.
You've prepared the query editor. Next, build the metric query.

In the **Metric** drop-down, paste `quickpizza_server_http_requests_total`, then select it from the list.

This counter tracks HTTP requests for QuickPizza services and includes a response **status** label.
blocks.tooltip: Paste the metric name, then pick it from the list.

blocks.content: In the **Label filters** row, open the **Label** drop-down and select **status**.
Open the operator drop-down and change **=** to **=~** so one filter can match every 5xx status code.
blocks.tooltip: =~ is regex match; = is exact match.

blocks.content:
In the **Select value** box, enter `5..`, then press Enter.

That regex matches any three-digit status that starts with 5.
blocks.tooltip: Enter 5.. and press Enter. Don't pick 500 from the list.

blocks.content: The metric is a counter that only increases. Add a range function to count new errors over the last 5 minutes. Optionally sum across services so the alert uses one total.

blocks.title: Add operations and run the query

blocks.content: Click **+ Operations**. In the **Operations** drop-down, select **Range functions / Increase**, then set the **Range** to **5m**.
Optionally, click **+ Operations** again and select **Aggregations / Sum**.

Check that your query matches `sum(increase(quickpizza_server_http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m]))` and that **Run queries** succeeds.

Next, confirm the alert condition.
In the **Alert condition** section, confirm **Is above** is selected and the value is **0**.

Click **Preview alert rule condition** to evaluate the condition against your query.

The result may show **Normal** or **Firing**, depending on whether the query is above **0** right now.
Your query and alert condition are set. Next, you create a folder and add labels.
